title: Haripuñjaya
capsule: Haripuñjaya was a Mon kingdom centered on the city of Lamphun in northern Thailand, legendarily founded around 661 by Queen Cāmadevī, who was sent from the Mon center of Lavo (Lopburi) to rule the newly established polity. The kingdom sustained Mon Buddhist culture in the northern uplands across roughly six centuries, during which its 48 rulers are listed in the chronicle Jinakālamālinī, though the record is dominated by religious building activities rather than military campaigns. Its end came in 1292 when Mangrai, king of Lan Na, besieged Lamphun after his agent Ai Fa spent seven years undermining the population's confidence in King Yība; Lamphun was incorporated into the Lan Na kingdom and its Mon population gradually assimilated.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's territorial extent is poorly documented; the core city and immediate hinterland (Lamphun basin) are certain, but the outer limits of political control are largely inferred from later Lan Na traditions and Mon settlement patterns.
